per_shot.note: Faceted segmented wyrm with spiny jaw reads as a serpent, but white-lavender body on a flat, overbright cyan pool has weak value contrast; jaw points up and away so the threat end is muted.
Nice crystalline facets and cyan spot-lights along the body; pool is a uniform glowing slab rather than brine depth, and the wyrm's own light barely registers against it.
Spiky violet-starburst tile sits in the rock as a distinct object; it neither reads as veinlight ore nor glows onto its neighbours, so neither the lure nor the 'light lands' rule works.

Crisp low-poly star crystal, on-palette ice/violet, but it is a flat decal on a purple square with no bloom spilling onto adjacent blocks and no subtle tell; it looks like a different pickup, not a beautiful ore.
Sea-green glow lands well on the dark rock, but the polyps are shapeless glowing half-domes clipping through tile edges; no tentacles, no mouth, nothing that reads as an animal or a hazard.
Close-up confirms blobs: a dome sliced by a tile seam and a hemisphere with no structure; good light pooling, no creature design.
Teal spiral reads as a galaxy against a starfield sky, not a current underwater; no eye visible, and the swimmer is jammed against the top HUD edge.
Pretty swirl but no eye, no centre of menace, and the dense starfield makes MAELIS look like space; nothing says 'creature' or 'danger'.

top_issues.issue: Riptide has no eye and reads as a space galaxy
top_issues.why: The creature is defined as a current with an eye; without the eye and with a starfield backdrop it is scenery, not a threat, and it breaks MAELIS's sea-green underwater mood.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Put a large faceted glowing eye at the vortex centre, replace the starfield with dark water and directional flow streaks, and keep the swimmer fully inside the frame.

top_issues.issue: Pressure Polyps are formless glowing domes
top_issues.why: Silhouette and dangerous end do not read at play size; the domes also clip through tile seams, which looks like a rendering error.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each polyp a mounted cap with a fringe of faceted tentacles or spines pointing at the play space, anchored cleanly to a rock face.

top_issues.issue: Frostbloom neither mimics veinlight ore nor lights the rock
top_issues.why: The brief wants a beautiful ore with a subtle tell; a violet star on a purple square reads as its own object and its glow stays inside its tile.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build it from the veinlight crack/glow language, add a soft cyan bloom that washes adjacent blocks, and keep the tell small (a faint pulse or a few petal-like spines).

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm pool is a flat bright slab that swallows the creature
top_issues.why: Uniform high-value cyan leaves no darkness for the wyrm's own glow to land on and lowers body contrast; it fights 'darkness as a mechanic'.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Darken the pool toward deep cyan with a brighter surface line and let the wyrm's spots and a head glow light the water and pool walls around it.

top_issues.why: The jaw angles up and away at play size, so the bite reads as decoration rather than a threat.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Orient the head along the swim direction with the open jaw and a warm or violet accent inside the mouth.

protect: Brinewyrm's faceted crystalline segments with cyan glow-spots
Polyps' sea-green light pooling onto surrounding dark rock
Riptide's teal swirl ribbons and the glowing segmented swimmer

Bigger faceted head, clear eye and visible teeth make the threat end legible; coil adds a strong silhouette; light still doesn't land because the water is already uniformly bright.
Identical to A: violet star tile that reads as its own pickup, not as veinlight ore, with no glow spilling onto neighbours.
Identical to A: crisp crystal but a flat decal on a purple square, no subtle tell and no landing light.
Three ceiling-hung polyps with caps, eye-spots and spiky faceted fringes read clearly as creatures with a dangerous underside; sea-green light pools on the rock above them.
Clean low-poly jellyfish-like silhouettes with drooping spines; on-palette sea-green, glow lands; spacing and anchoring are tidy.
Faceted glowing eye anchors the vortex and flow streaks show the current; dark backdrop replaces the starfield; swimmer sits in frame with its own halo. Little light from the eye lands on the rock.
Strong read: a slit-pupil eye in a crystalline ring at the centre of a spiralling current; streaks give motion; eye is a touch icy-cyan against MAELIS sea-green but works as an accent.

top_issues.issue: Riptide's eye light doesn't land on the surroundings
top_issues.why: The eye is the brightest thing in the frame but the rock and floor below show little of its light, so it floats like a UI element.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a soft sea-green/cyan point light from the eye that washes the nearby floor and the swirl ribbons, and pull the eye hue slightly toward sea-green.

top_issues.issue: Polyps' habitat rock is nearly black and featureless
top_issues.why: Outside the polyp halos the rock gives almost no faceted structure, so the creatures sit on a void rather than in MAELIS stone.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the polyp glow catch faceted edges and a little nacre sheen on the ceiling blocks they hang from.
